turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's not waste it. Why did my son find out about a zero from his phone in the middle of class?
Don't thank me yet. Answer the question, Hale: who decided on a zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?
Owen is a great kid. Really bright, one of my favourites.
"Don't manage me." He's a great kid with a zero in the gradebook. I asked who decided and whether anyone spoke to him first.
I'm sure this is all just a misunderstanding.
"Probably" and "just a misunderstanding." Okay. A misunderstanding doesn't put a zero in the gradebook, so I'll ask a third time: who decided, and was Owen heard first?
So can we agree he's a good student?
You're leading me, Hale. I've done this for twenty years, and my son's grades are in the gradebook where you put them. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen first?
